solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Asian deity placed river by a river in Asia

indicators.note: by means beside, so the last short piece is set right next to what comes before it

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A god is set down beside a river in some Asian land.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'river' is just R; the second is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brahmaputra flows through Tibet, India and Bangladesh, a major waterway of the continent.

clue.text: Maybe John‘s fitting in again, given time

indicators.note: something put in another word sits inside its letters

blocks.note: bis is Latin for twice, used in music and encores for again
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: John's outfit fits him again after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of John's stands for is. John the Baptist is the obvious example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: John the Baptist is the famous bearer of this title, so a specific person illustrates the general word.

clue.text: Enchanting remark from a villain wearing a pair of undergarments

indicators.note: the villain is dressed in the garments, so those letters wrap around

blocks.note: the first a, taken as written
a cad is a dishonourable man
the second a, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rogue in two items of lingerie says something charming.
explanation.walkthrough: The villain together with the second a is put between the two bras, and the first a goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Abracadabra is the word a conjuror says while casting a spell, literally a remark that enchants.

clue.text: Think of the late or early period in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word is matched by its sound alone

blocks.note: morn is the early part of the day

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether to stay up late or rise early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The late' looks like a time of day to contrast with early, but it means the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve is to dwell sorrowfully on those who have died, the late being the deceased.

clue.text: Clip up court robes if high official there

blocks.note: all sixteen letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Robes are hitched up in court when a senior lawyer appears.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram word: the instruction to clip up the robes, to rearrange them, is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A state prosecuting lawyer is a senior legal officer who brings criminal cases on behalf of the public.

clue.text: Landed up penning composer’s moving account?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals

blocks.note: landed as in got hold of

explanation.surface: Someone has written a touching account of a composer's life.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving looks emotional but means on the move, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or book about journeys is literally an account of moving about from place to place.

clue.text: Addresses a set of lines in mail briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter
the set of lines goes inside the shortened word

blocks.note: post is the British word for mail
a strophe is a stanza of a poem or ode

explanation.surface: Someone sends a short poem in a letter to several addresses.
explanation.walkthrough: Addresses is a plural noun here: an apostrophe is a speech addressed to someone absent or dead.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric, an apostrophe is a passage turning aside to speak directly to an absent person or thing.

clue.text: Battle line’s cut in retreat

indicators.note: cut in means inserted into the middle

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: An army's front line is broken during a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after line stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking flight means running away, so the noun is a hasty withdrawal from danger.

clue.text: Suspect roughly apprehended in case of felony

indicators.note: apprehended means caught and held, so one piece is held inside another
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A suspect is roughly arrested in a felony case.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspect looks like a noun for an arrested person, but the definition is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that seems dubious or arouses distrust is informally said to smell of fish.

clue.text: Below River Test, one last character with lots of works?

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
zed is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Something sits below the River Test, a Hampshire trout stream, with a final figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Test is a famous English chalk stream, so 'River Test' reads as one name; it splits into two. Below just places the pieces in order down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A developed manufacturing economy has many factories, and works is another word for factories.

clue.text: “Hello, sailor” is appropriate

blocks.note: jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Greeting a sailor is said to be the proper thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Appropriate is a verb here, to seize, not the adjective proper.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize a vehicle or take over something by force is to appropriate it for yourself.

clue.text: With Bill following, say “I’m shocked!”

indicators.note: following means placed after, which fixes the order of the two pieces

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
a bill is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: Someone receives a bill and exclaims in horror.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned mild oath expressing surprise, a minced form of 'by God'.

clue.text: Nearly go out and attack poor child

blocks.note: a candle gutters when it flickers and is close to dying
to snipe is to attack with sly criticism or gunfire

explanation.surface: Someone almost leaves the house and then assaults a needy youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A guttersnipe is a ragged slum child who lives on the streets, hence a poor youngster.

clue.text: Mimic US writer, an unknown Kansan

blocks.note: to do someone is to impersonate them
algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns

explanation.surface: An impersonator copies an American author and a nobody from Kansas.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a single person: the heroine of The Wizard of Oz comes from Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy Gale, heroine of The Wizard of Oz, lives on a Kansas farm, so she is the famous example.

clue.text: Fashionable label brought back maybe crude design

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: crude oil is an example of oil

explanation.surface: A trendy label has revived a rough-looking pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: Crude looks like an adjective for design, but it stands for oil, of which crude is a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An intaglio is an engraved or incised figure, a carved pattern sunk into stone or metal.

clue.text: Worry for each kind of wine knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means sent backwards, so the word is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone frets about drinking a glass of wine for each person.
explanation.walkthrough: Knocked back suggests downing a drink, but it signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone or make them anxious is to trouble their peace of mind.

clue.text: Set off, with a way to cross river

indicators.note: the way crosses the river by spanning it, lying either side

blocks.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Travellers depart, taking a road that crosses a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Set off looks like starting a journey, but it means stirred or triggered.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off feelings is to stir or awaken them, so the past participle describes something stirred up.

clue.text: Steward to go off, returning on time for resolution

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
in an across clue, on means placed after the next piece

blocks.note: Jan 1, New Year's Day, with the numeral as I, is when resolutions are made

explanation.surface: A steward heads back to settle a dispute in time.
explanation.walkthrough: Resolution suggests settling a dispute, but here it is the New Year kind, and the 1 of Jan 1 is written as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker of a building, especially in Scotland and the US, looks after and keeps it, much as a steward does.

clue.text: Secretly touring some countries in wild fashion

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: inly is an archaic word for inwardly, privately
a continent is made up of several countries

explanation.surface: A traveller covertly tours several nations in an unruly way.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means without self-restraint, especially in passion, so it describes unbridled, unruly behaviour.

clue.text: Service dispatched, carrying ace stuff

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: A tennis serve is sent over containing first-rate material.
explanation.walkthrough: Service and ace suggest tennis, but service is a religious rite.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a religious ceremony such as baptism or the Eucharist, a church service.

clue.text: House staff do twirls

indicators.note: twirls means spins round, so the letters face the other way

blocks.note: ut is the old name for the note do in sol-fa

explanation.surface: Members of a household's staff spin round at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: House means royal dynasty, as with the House of Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I, a ruling family or house.

clue.text: Artist to draw depressing image of existence

blocks.note: to trace is to draw over outlines

explanation.surface: A painter sets out to sketch a gloomy scene of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase pictures modern working life as rodents running endlessly in competition, a bleak view of the daily grind.

clue.text: In the main, it’s outstanding publicity with name on the right

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed next, after the earlier piece

blocks.note: a promo is a promotional piece
N is the abbreviation for name
Tories are the British Conservatives, the political right

explanation.surface: Mostly, outstanding publicity carries a right-wing name.
explanation.walkthrough: In the main seems to mean mostly, but the main is the sea, and outstanding means sticking out.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland juts out into the sea, so it stands out from the coast into the open water.

clue.text: I’m grateful to get recurrent pain in bones

explanation.surface: Someone is oddly thankful for an ache that keeps coming back in their bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsi are the ankle bones, a group of small skeletal parts in the foot.

clue.text: Jet circles area, quiet or loud?

indicators.note: circles means goes round, so one word surrounds the others

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A jet circling overhead: is it silent or noisy?
explanation.walkthrough: Loud here means gaudy, as in a loud shirt, not noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud clothes are garish and showy, so the word means ostentatious.

clue.text: Hospital worker puts up with wood that’s cut

blocks.note: a porter moves patients round a hospital
to put someone up is to house them

explanation.surface: A hospital worker shelters guests and has some timber that has been sawn.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut means a cut of meat, not something sawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A porterhouse is a large cut of beef from the loin, a particular joint from the butcher.

clue.text: Without hesitation, making free drink

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

explanation.surface: Someone unhesitatingly offers free drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Free looks like an adjective for the drink but is the noun for setting free, minus the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A libation is an offering of drink poured out to a god, and jokingly any alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Smoker to get over source of discomfort

blocks.note: lum is Scots for a chimney, which smokes
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A smoker wants to get over some ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The smoker is a chimney, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is lower-back pain, a common physical complaint that causes aches.

clue.text: Power to hurt a biologist, not European chemist

indicators.note: not European means drop the abbreviation for European

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for power
an ecologist is a kind of biologist

explanation.surface: A powerful scientist could harm a fellow biologist from outside Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The E that goes is the first letter of ecologist, not any E.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacologist studies drugs and their effects, and chemist in Britain also means a pharmacist.

clue.text: Time to move inelegantly in pants

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: It is time to shuffle awkwardly about in trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like trousers or underwear but is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, pants means nonsense or rubbish, as does silly empty talk.

clue.text: I collect PayPal transfers in fury

indicators.note: transfers suggests letters moved to new places

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone collecting online payments is enraged by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplectic means purple with rage, so the adverb describes doing something furiously angry.

clue.text: One’s very sharp at English exam, amazingly

indicators.note: amazingly means in a surprising way, hinting at a wild rearrangement

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A clever student does brilliantly in an English exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Very sharp suggests a clever pupil, but it is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher's cleaver has a keen edge, so it is a literally sharp tool for chopping.

clue.text: Hopeless sort of computer game is included in trial

indicators.note: is included in means placed inside another word

blocks.note: a trial is a nuisance, a pest
a sim is a simulation game

explanation.surface: A gloomy gamer's computer game is part of a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Trial looks like a test, but it means an annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimist always expects the worst and lacks hope, so they are a gloomy, despairing type.

clue.text: Possessing urge, laugh? This creature might

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so one word is held inside another

explanation.surface: Seized by an urge, might this animal laugh?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reaches back to laugh: this creature might laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is famous for its cackling call, which sounds like human laughter.

clue.text: Home cover’s included fairly

indicators.note: included means put inside, so one piece sits within another

explanation.surface: A home's insurance is fairly comprehensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where an animal or plant lives, its natural dwelling place.

clue.text: Filling of jam, plenty or enough?

indicators.note: filling of means what lies inside, so the letters come from within the next words

explanation.surface: Is there plenty of jam in the sandwich, or just enough?
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means more than sufficient, a generous quantity that is plenty for the need.

clue.text: The last word in divine pickle

indicators.note: in means placed inside another word

explanation.surface: Someone has the final say in a holy mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Divine is a verb, to foresee, not the adjective holy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a pickle means being in a difficult situation, a tight spot or plight.

clue.text: Like certain characters in drug affair

blocks.note: an affair is a case, a matter

explanation.surface: Some shady characters are mixed up in a drugs scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters means letters, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters are kept in the top case of a printer's type, so the phrase describes them.

clue.text: Judge turned up on pitch

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top
in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece

explanation.surface: An umpire arrives at the cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reads the same either way, so here 'turned up' just restores it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rater assesses and grades things, just as a judge gives an assessment of quality.

clue.text: Leader of air force about to release bold lady

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
about means around, so one word surrounds another

blocks.note: to vent is to let out

explanation.surface: An Air Force commander is about to free a daring woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Air force looks like one term, but air gives only its first letter and force is a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventuress is a woman who seeks wealth or position by daring and unscrupulous means.

clue.text: Recover or recovered like books?

blocks.note: first meaning: to bounce back from a setback
second meaning: given a fresh binding, as old volumes are

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is split as re-bound: books whose covers have been renewed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bounce back after misfortune is to rebound, and a book given a new cover has been re-bound.

clue.text: Quail if nude modelling without right attributes

indicators.note: modelling means shaping, as clay is reshaped into a new form

blocks.note: all eleven letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks from posing naked, lacking the right qualities for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the necessary qualifications means not having the proper credentials or skills for the role.

clue.text: Caring too much to evict and reprove criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or corrupt, so letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A smothering parent wants to kick out and scold an offender.
explanation.definitionFit: An overprotective parent shields a child excessively, showing excessive concern for their safety.

clue.text: Moderate starter of pâté the only thing I consumed

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dieter eats only a little pâté as a starter, by way of moderation.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter suggests the first course of a meal, but it means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease or lessen something such as pain without curing it, so to moderate it.

clue.text: Fashionably petite and fit one, that Parisian

blocks.note: a fit, as of coughing, is a bout
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A slim, fit Parisian woman is admired.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit looks like healthy or attractive, but it is a noun, a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, the word describes a small, exclusive and stylish business, like a little dress shop.

clue.text: Blasted husband loves making a fuss

blocks.note: bally is a British euphemism for bloody
H is the abbreviation for husband
love is zero in tennis, written O; two of them

explanation.surface: A wretched husband loves creating a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo means noisy publicity or uproar, a big commotion about something.

clue.text: Feel anger for one half of match, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means as spoken, so the word goes by sound alone

blocks.note: a wedding is a match, and the bride is one of its two halves; bridal means of the bride

explanation.surface: One side in a game seethes with anger.
explanation.walkthrough: Match looks like a sports contest but means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to show resentment or anger, like a horse tossing its head against the reins.

clue.text: One’s blown bonus eating goose

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so one word swallows another

blocks.note: a boon is a welcome benefit
a goose and an ass are both fools

explanation.surface: Someone squanders a bonus on a goose dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Blown looks like money wasted, but the instrument is played by blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: The bassoon is a woodwind instrument played by blowing through a double reed.

clue.text: Rock star isn’t in school

indicators.note: rock means shake, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rock star is not at school.
explanation.definitionFit: St Trinian's is the fictional girls' school of Ronald Searle's cartoons and the comedy films.

clue.text: Follow is about right for this

indicators.note: is about means goes round, so the word surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tracker is told to keep to the right while following a path.
explanation.walkthrough: Follow does double duty: it gives the outer word and is also the definition of the result, which 'this' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to track or pursue them from behind, closely shadowing their movements.

clue.text: Clothing on show

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
to wear a look or expression is to show it

explanation.surface: Garments are put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: Clothing on show reads as a fashion display, but on and show are each pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Legwear covers stockings, tights and trousers, a general term for garments worn below the waist.

clue.text: Proust novel‘s dull quality

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Proust novel is notoriously long and boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a noun, one of Proust's books, but works as an adjective, new.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness or dazed lethargy, a dulled condition of mind.

clue.text: Government supporter in charge, in fact

blocks.note: i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A backer of government is actually in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistic is a numerical datum, a figure presented as a piece of hard information.

clue.text: Stepping on court game’s dividing lines

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means coming after the next piece

blocks.note: doubles is the tennis game for pairs

explanation.surface: Someone pacing a tennis court is studying its marked lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Dividing lines suggests the court markings, but it means spacing lines of text apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Typing with a blank line between each line of text keeps lines separated on the page.

clue.text: Legendary friend, one who wanders up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A mythical companion is a wanderer who turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: Damon and Pythias are the Greek legend's pattern of loyal friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon offered his life as surety for Pythias in the Greek tale, a byword for loyal comradeship.

clue.text: A couple of leaves, or as many as you want

explanation.surface: Two leaves, or as many as you like, from a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like foliage, but it is the verb, departs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from French means in abundance, aplenty, as much as one desires.

clue.text: Bow’s straight with recording for a dance

indicators.note: Bow is a Cockney district of East London, where speakers drop their aitches

explanation.surface: An archer's bow is kept straight as a recording plays for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is not a weapon or a curtsy but the East End district, so the H goes as a Cockney would say it.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ballroom dance of the early twentieth century, done to ragtime.

clue.text: Youngster redeveloping the London borough

indicators.note: redeveloping means rebuilding, so the letters are reassembled

blocks.note: a lamb is a young sheep or child

explanation.surface: A young person is rebuilding part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambeth is a district of south London on the Thames, home to Lambeth Palace.

clue.text: Desire this person has to be caustic

blocks.note: I've, from the setter's point of view

explanation.surface: Someone admits their lust makes them sharp-tongued.
explanation.definitionFit: Something caustic burns away surfaces, as acid does, wearing them down gradually.

clue.text: It’s formed by a group of signatories?

definitions.text: It’s formed by a group of signatories?

indicators.note: formed by part of the next word means the letters come from within it

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: An alliance is created by countries signing a treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and a group of the letters of the last word gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization was created by states that signed the 1949 treaty.

clue.text: Caught fabric in drawer

blocks.note: c is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth got snagged in a chest drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: Drawer is not a piece of furniture but something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured stick of wax is used to draw pictures, so it is a drawing tool.

clue.text: Person seeking return in cattle pen

explanation.surface: Someone wants to get back into a cattle enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: Return means a financial yield, not going back.
explanation.definitionFit: A shareholder invests capital expecting a dividend or profit on the investment.
